findings.issue: The 60s capture timeout is armed before startCapture and is never disarmed after revealWhenPainted() confirms the UI is ready (:142-165). It therefore bounds the entire interactive annotation session, not just a silent startup failure: a user who spends more than 60s selecting/annotating is endCapture()d mid-edit, the selection is discarded, and main falls back to the legacy controller (main.js:245-246). This is bounded and recoverable, but it is a new user-visible abort introduced by the fix; the unit timeout test uses 20ms and does not exercise post-ready editing.
findings.evidence: app/main/screenshot-library.js:18 (DEFAULT_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS=60000), :38-42 (armTimer), :41 (timeout -> failPending), :48 (clear only in settle), :142-165 (revealWhenPainted returns without clearing the timer), :182 (armTimer before startCapture); app/main/main.js:245-246 (legacy fallback on any non-ok/non-cancelled result); app/main/screenshot-library.unit.test.js:203-210 (20ms timeout test).
findings.required_fix: Clear or disable the interaction timeout once revealWhenPainted() succeeds (windowClosed/ok/cancel still settle the capture) or make the post-ready timeout explicitly long/documented; add a test that a capture remains pending past the configured timeout after the UI is ready.

findings.issue: onSave clears the pending timeout for the whole native save-dialog lifetime and only re-arms it if the dialog resolves cancelled (:106). If the native dialog never resolves or is not visible, the capture stays pending with all app windows hidden and imageWorkflow.busy=true indefinitely. The wrapper also does not mirror the third-party library's setAlwaysOnTop(false)/true around the dialog, even though the dialog's parent is the always-on-top kiosk screenshot window, so an obscured dialog is plausible (unverified on Windows in this locked session).
findings.evidence: app/main/screenshot-library.js:88-118 (clearTimeout at :92, showSaveDialog at :96, re-arm only at :106); app/node_modules/electron-screenshots/lib/index.js:305,317 (library toggles alwaysOnTop around its own save dialog); app/node_modules/electron-screenshots/lib/index.js:126-162 (screenshot window is alwaysOnTop and kiosk); inline probe with a never-resolving dialog and timeoutMs=30: settled=false, petVisible=false, ends=0 after the timeout would have fired.
findings.required_fix: Mirror the library's always-on-top toggle around the dialog (restore on both resolve and reject), and either keep a bounded save-dialog timeout (settle capture-failed so main falls back) or cancel the capture when the screenshot window closes. Add a unit case with a never-resolving dialog.

findings.issue: Duplicate save events are not guarded. onSave checks pending/settling, but settling is only set in endAndSettle after the dialog resolves (:55-63), so two SCREENSHOTS:save events before then both open native save dialogs. The wrapper eventually settles once, but the second dialog is orphaned. This is the remaining hole in the duplicate-event guard (ok/cancel are covered).
findings.evidence: app/main/screenshot-library.js:88-96 (no saving flag; settling is set only at :57); app/main/screenshot-library.unit.test.js:156-169 (duplicate ok only), :171-199 (single save events); inline probe: dialogs after duplicate save = 2, capture settled once via cancel.
findings.required_fix: Add a save-in-progress guard (a saving flag or set settling before opening the dialog) so duplicate save events are preventDefault/no-op, and add a duplicate-save unit test.

findings.issue: The save-cancel test and the docs state that canceling Save keeps the capture UI usable, but the prebuilt UI resets the selection and toolbar in the renderer immediately after sending SCREENSHOTS:save, before the dialog result. On cancel the wrapper correctly keeps the capture pending and re-arms the timer, but the user must make a new selection; the unit test's manual cancel event does not model this renderer reset.
findings.required_fix: Correct the test/docs wording (the capture remains open but the selection is cleared), or provide a recovery affordance if the stock reset is not acceptable.

residual_risks: Locked Windows session: the post-fix screen runtime (app/main/screenshot-library.runtime.test.js, screenshot-p3.runtime.test.js, screenshot-native.runtime.test.js) and the portable exe smoke could not be run (Graphics.CopyFromScreen returns 'invalid handle'). The code and 41/41 unit suite are sound, but the worker-fed default capture, warm second-capture timings, real Save button/dialog behavior, hide-before-capture compositor behavior, and the rebuilt portable remain unverified after the fixes.

The Save path bounds normal use, but the native save dialog is trusted to resolve: the pending timeout is cleared while it is open and main's fallback is not reached until it resolves. If the dialog is obscured (always-on-top/kiosk parent; the wrapper does not mirror the library's setAlwaysOnTop(false) toggle) or hangs, the capture can stay pending with app windows hidden; pressing Esc on the focused dialog should cancel it, but this is not proven in the locked session.

The 60s timeout also caps interactive annotation; a slow user can lose an in-progress selection and be switched to the legacy screenshot UI (R2-01). This is bounded and recoverable, not a permanent lock.

The no-flash property is still only documented, not fixed: the library shows its transparent window before the frozen image is sent/painted (revealWhenPainted only checks after the fact), and the setOpacity workaround was reverted. No high-speed capture was performed.

The default library path is single-display (cursor display) by design; the worker-fed dipToScreenRect -> physical bounds mapping and the frozen-image crop/text scaling were validated on the 100% primary display pre-fix, not on the 125% secondary and not post-fix.

The wrapper's hide() of app windows is not followed by a compositor wait; the worker captures immediately, so a pet/settings ghost in the frozen image was not observed but is not asserted, and the post-fix runtime that would assert it is blocked.

Real-provider claims (multimodal flag change, config.json.bak-vision-1793184768201, one real vision call, four real ASR calls) were not independently reverified: no real calls were made and the user profile was not read. The hermetic gate/mock passed; the frozen evidence is only code-consistent.

The portable artifact app/dist-exe/Voice2Prompt-1.0.0-Portable.exe is the pre-fix build; docs correctly mark it as not final, but it must be rebuilt and smoked after unlock. asar:false exposes plain source/node_modules in the package (accepted for this local build).

The unit suite covers the wrapper but not the Electron integration of the new captureImage override; the lock/fallback behavior of the real library UI with the wrapper (including real save-dialog presentation) depends on the blocked runtime test.
The node-screenshots and uiohook-napi native x64 Windows binaries tie the portable to that ABI/OS; unrelated to this fix but still a delivery constraint.
